title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a short scratch computation, written on the verso of a typescript page of SGA 7, exposé IX (the mirror-image typescript and the page numbers 398/399 come from that text, not from this computation).

Setting. There are two abelian categories, C and M_ω, with left exact functors σ: C → M_ω and ψ: M_ω → C. M_ω is presumably a category of modules over ω, a de Rham–type or divided-power algebra, given the cote; the page itself does not say. The structure is:
- σ ⊣ ψ, with unit id_C → ψσ an isomorphism. The first attempt 'ψσ = id' is crossed out and replaced by 'ψσ ≃← id_C'.
- A counit σψ → id_{M_ω}.

So σ is a fully faithful left adjoint. Grothendieck passes to derived functors Rσ: D+(C) → D+(M_ω) and Rψ: D+(M_ω) → D+(C), and asks (marked '?') whether the derived adjunction Hom(RσK, L) ≃ Hom(K, RψL) holds.

The two maps.
- Forward: apply Rψ to get Hom(RσK, L) → Hom(RψRσK, RψL). Then use RψRσ ≃ R(ψσ) ≃ id, which needs σ to send injectives to ψ-acyclics, to land in Hom(K, RψL).
- Backward: apply Rσ to get Hom(K, RψL) → Hom(RσK, RσRψL). Then use RσRψ ≃ R(σψ) and the derived counit RσRψL → L to land in Hom(RσK, L).
- The bottom pair of vertical arrows records the counits RσRψRσK → RσK and RσRψL → L that are needed to check that the two maps are mutually inverse (triangle identities).

Conclusion. 'D+C → D+M_ω pl[einement] fid[èle], compatible avec multiplication': the derived functor Rσ is fully faithful, since Hom(K, K') ≃ Hom(K, RψRσK') ≃ Hom(RσK, RσK'), and it is compatible with the multiplicative (tensor) structures. This is presumably meant to embed a derived category of, e.g., crystals or modules into a derived category of modules over a divided-power de Rham–type object.
errors: The identifications RψRσ ≃ R(ψσ) and RσRψ ≃ R(σψ) require acyclicity hypotheses: σ must send injectives to ψ-acyclics, and ψ must send injectives to σ-acyclics. These are not stated on the page.
That the forward and backward maps are inverse needs the derived triangle identities. These are only sketched by the counit arrows at the bottom.

Hom(RσK, L) ≃ Hom(K, RψL) is not literally a derived adjunction unless Rσ is computed as a derived functor compatible with the adjunction. For a left adjoint one would normally expect a left derived functor; deriving σ on the right is unusual unless σ is exact. The '?' shows Grothendieck himself was unsure.
'Compatible avec multiplication' is asserted without any argument.

ideas.what: Derived functors of an adjoint pair whose unit is an isomorphism give a fully faithful derived functor (a derived embedding).
ideas.modern_name: Derived adjunction / fully faithful derived functor (colocalization)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard derived-category material (Verdier, Hartshorne's Residues and Duality)
ideas.where_published: Standard; similar arguments appear in SGA 4 / Hartshorne RD

ideas.what: Embedding D+(C) fully faithfully into D+ of modules over a de Rham / divided-power object, compatibly with tensor structures.
ideas.modern_name: Comparison between derived categories of crystals and of modules over a (divided power) de Rham complex
ideas.usually_credited_to: Berthelot, Ogus, Illusie (crystalline cohomology, late 1970s); later Bhatt–Lurie / Drinfeld (prismatization)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine scratch check of a derived adjunction and full faithfulness. Without the context of what C and M_ω are, nothing here goes beyond standard homological algebra.
transcription_corrections: The bottom vertical arrows are the counit maps RσRψRσK → RσK and RσRψL → L.
The line 'D+C → D+M_ω' refers to Rσ.
The underbrace under RσRψ(L) reads R(σψ)(L); the one under RψRσK reads R(ψσ)(K) ≃ K.
The typed text visible through the paper is SGA 7 exposé IX (verso bleed-through). It is not part of these notes.
